text:
Parker Wotherspoon's season restarted on Nov 11, when Vegas activated him off injured reserve (according to Daily Faceoff). Two nights later against Nashville he picked up an assist, his first point since coming back, on 20.9 minutes, as RotoWire noted. It's a small sample: 8 games, 1 point.

The points have never been the point with him. A 2015 fourth-round pick by the Islanders, he took the long road through the AHL, then had 30 points in 80 games for Pittsburgh last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him 72nd of 215 defensemen with 500-plus minutes, worth 1.0 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. In Vegas the early process is excellent: the Golden Knights have had 59.9% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 8 points better than without him. They've also scored 4.35 fewer goals than those chances deserved while he's out there, which is why his line looks quiet. The thing to watch is his ice time as he settles back in.
headline: Wotherspoon is back, and Vegas is winning his minutes
